subject: Ansible-first approach for Helm + Terraform convergence — state migration & rollback playbook
messages:
From: David Li <david.li@acmeinfra.com>
To: vanessa_ortiz@redwood.com
Cc: infra@acme.com
Date: Tue, 14 Apr 2026 15:02:00 -0700
Subject: Proposal: Ansible-first orchestration for Helm + Terraform convergence

Vanessa,

Thanks again for the sync last week. As promised, I pulled together a short proposal for an "Ansible-first" orchestration layer that sequences Terraform and Helm operations for on-prem/private VPC rolls. High-level goals:

- Keep Terraform as the source of truth for long-lived infra (VPC, subnets, LB, DNS).
- Use Helm/Helmfile for app-level artefacts and CRDs, coordinated by Ansible playbooks to ensure ordering and idempotency.
- Add a state-migration plan to move TF remote state from S3-style bucket to our Vault-backed backend + DynamoDB-style locking (we'll call it "vault-locker").
- Provide a lightweight rollback playbook that can reverse Helm releases and re-apply last-good TF state snapshot.

I've attached three artifacts: ansible-runbooks-v1.md (runbook drafts), tf-state-migration-plan.yaml (migration steps + prechecks), and a diagram illustrating the recommended ordering.

Questions for you and your infra team:
1) Are there existing constraints on IP retention for the customer clusters (we saw some notes about fixed-bounce gateway IPs)?
2) Any policy that forbids agent-based orchestration on the bastion hosts?

If it helps, I'm available to run a short walkthrough with your team tomorrow morning.

Best,
David
David Li
Principal Systems Engineer | ACME Infra Solutions

From: vanessa_ortiz@redwood.com
To: David Li <david.li@acmeinfra.com>
Cc: marissa_cole@redwood.com, grace_oconnor@redwood.com
Date: Wed, 15 Apr 2026 09:14:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Proposal: Ansible-first orchestration for Helm + Terraform convergence

David —

Thanks for the write-up and the attachments. This direction looks promising. Quick answers up-front:

- IP retention: for regulated customers we often need stable egress IPs for allowlists. That box is checked for ACME accounts we plan to migrate.
- Agent on bastion: our security team prefers push-based runbooks (Ansible over SSH) rather than running persistent agents in the management plane.

Can we run through the migration prechecks with the team today at 11 PT? I'll loop in Lauren to confirm the compliance checklist and Marissa for CI gating.

Action items for the 11am sync:
- Walk the tf-state-migration precheck sequence (what's backed up, how we snapshot)
- Confirm Helm release ordering and whether CRDs are applied in a separate pass or baked into the same chart rollouts
- Agree on the rollback story: what things are reversible automatically vs. manual steps (DB schema changes, service-account secrets)

Thanks — I cc'd Lauren so she sees the compliance angle.

—Vanessa
Vanessa Ortiz
Senior Product Manager, Private Deployments | Redwood Inference

From: marissa_cole@redwood.com
To: vanessa_ortiz@redwood.com, grace_oconnor@redwood.com
Cc: lauren_bishop@redwood.com
Date: Wed, 15 Apr 2026 11:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Proposal: Ansible-first orchestration for Helm + Terraform convergence

Short notes from the sync:

- CI gating: we want a two-stage pipeline. Stage A (terraform plan + static policy checks via tfsec/OPA) must pass before Stage B (ansible orchestrator triggers helm templates + helm diff checks).
- Locking: we will require remote state locking with a migration window and an enforced freeze period (no manual terraform applies) during cutover. David: can the "vault-locker" provide per-workspace locks?
- Helm CRDs: prefer a separate CRD-first pass; templates that depend on CRDs should be gated to the post-CRD release to avoid install-time errors.
- Rollback: propose a document-based rollback playbook where Ansible references a single JSON artifact containing the last-known-good values for Helm + an S3 snapshot pointer for TF state.

Marissa
Senior Infrastructure Engineer | Redwood Inference

From: David Li <david.li@acmeinfra.com>
To: vanessa_ortiz@redwood.com
Cc: marissa_cole@redwood.com, grace_oconnor@redwood.com, lauren_bishop@redwood.com
Date: Fri, 16 Apr 2026 09:28:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Proposal: Ansible-first orchestration for Helm + Terraform convergence

Thanks team — good meeting today. Follow-ups and commitments from ACME side: 

- Vault-locker supports per-workspace locks and exposes a short API for Ansible to acquire/release locks. We'll ship a small Ansible module (acquire_lock/release_lock) with the runbooks.
- TF state migration: we'll provide a migration playbook that performs: 1) snapshot current backend, 2) run terraform init -migrate-state to new backend in a dry-run mode, 3) verify resource diffs with a compare script, 4) cutover in reserved window. The migration artifact tf-state-migration-plan.yaml (attached) includes prechecks and a rollback step that re-populates previous backend if needed.
- Helm ordering: we'll provide helm-chart-ordering-diagram.png and a recommended two-pass release (CRD-only pass, then app charts). We recommend versioned CRD bundles per-cluster to reduce drift.
- Attachments: ansible-runbooks-v1.md (detailed runbooks + example playbook snippets), tf-state-migration-plan.yaml, helm-chart-ordering-diagram.png. I'll also attach a small sample Ansible module next week.

Next steps: ACME will open a tracking ticket with your infra team and provide the Ansible module in the repo linked here: https://github.com/acme/ansible-modules/tree/vault-locker. Let's tentatively schedule the migration dry-run for May 8 (prod freeze window) pending compliance approval.

David
Principal Systems Engineer | ACME Infra Solutions
